title: The Harry James session with Basie men and John Hammond
summary: Harry James, then with Benny Goodman, used Basie sidemen for her first New York date. The titles included 'The Song of the Wanderer', and Dance gives the personnel. Humes calls it the only session she really enjoyed.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, I see. Well, that session with Harry James, Harry didn't have his own band?
No.
Was he with Benny then?
Yeah, he was with Benny, but he used alot of the Basie boys.
Oh, did he?
Sweets, he had Buck Clayton.
I'll tell you what, I've got the personnel on that just let me get it.
(Went off record.)
Helen, we want to talk about that record session. And I know the personnel now.
The one with Harry James?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

The one with Harry James. And the personnel is Buck Clayton and Herschel Evans, Earl Warren, Eddie Durham, Jack Washington, and Walter Page and Jo Jones. And your titles, "The Song of the Wanderer", and that was sensational.
Oh yes, everybody liked that.
Everybody liked that. And then you did "I Can Dream, Can't I".
Yeah.
And "It's The Dreamer In Me", and "Jubilee". And that was a wonderful session, wasn't it?
Yes it was. And I enjoyed it so. That was the first session that I think I made that I really enjoyed. Well, that was the only session I made that I really enjoyed.
What studio, do you remember?
No, I don't know what studio.
It was a session that John had engineered somewhere?
Yes. You know, John, he was so nice and he just seemed to, well I didn't know nothing about

him. He was nice you know. He just seemed to be right in there with them.
Yeah, and you could tell he was very enthusiastic about what you were doing.
That's right.
